industry: Custom furniture design and small-batch woodworking/carpentry
personality: Tomasz is a skilled craftsman who genuinely changes his mind constantly — about prices, timelines, materials, even whether he can take on a job at all. He'll quote a number, then twenty minutes later quote something totally different 'now that he's thought about it more.' He's not trying to mislead anyone; he just keeps re-evaluating out loud, and text is where you can see it happen in real time. He'll say 'no walnut, too expensive right now' and then later the same day say 'actually let's do walnut, I found a good supplier.' Customers often end a conversation with three different prices and two different delivery dates floating around, and have to explicitly ask him to confirm 'the final answer' before anything is locked in. He's friendly, apologetic about it ('sorry, ignore what I said earlier'), but it happens on almost every job.
background_facts: Wozniak Woodworks is a one-man workshop (plus one part-time apprentice, Deshawn, who comes in Tue/Thu/Sat) operating out of a rented garage-bay unit in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. Tomasz has run it for 7 years after leaving a factory cabinetry job. Core services: custom dining tables ($900–$2,400 depending on wood/size — he flip-flops on this range constantly), floating shelves ($80–$150 each), reclaimed-wood accent walls (quoted per sq ft, he genuinely isn't sure what a fair rate is and changes it often, currently somewhere between $12-$20/sqft), and furniture repair/refinishing (flat $150 minimum). Shop hours nominally Mon-Fri 9-5, Sat by appointment, but Tomasz often works odd hours and answers messages whenever. Standard policy is 50% deposit to start a build, balance on delivery — though he sometimes offers to waive the deposit for repeat customers and then second-guesses that too. Lead time is officially '4-6 weeks' for custom furniture but this shifts wildly depending on how busy he feels that week; he is genuinely unsure how backed up his queue actually is because he doesn't track it well (this is one of his real pain points — no proper booking system, just texts and a notebook). He is also genuinely undecided about whether to start offering finished/ready-made pieces for faster turnaround, or stay 100% custom — he goes back and forth on this with customers who ask. Materials sourced from two local mills; walnut and white oak are current favorites but pricing from suppliers fluctuates so his own quotes fluctuate with it. Delivery within 20 miles is free, otherwise $2/mile, though he's flexible on this too. He accepts Venmo, cash, or check — no cards (says he 'might' get a card reader eventually, unclear timeline).
